chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said:

When you arrive at a land and you intend to stay in it for ten days, so fast and complete (the prayers); and if you intend to stay for less than ten days, so break (do not fast) what is between you and the month. So when it reaches a month, so complete the prayers and the fasts, even if you say, 'I shall be leaving tomorrow'.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules of prayer and fasting for a traveler intending to stay in a city for ten days or less?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the ten-day rule (iqamah) for travelers, distinguishing between the shortened prayers of a traveler and the full obligations of a resident. It specifically addresses the nuance of fasting, noting that while short stays exempt one from fasting, extending the stay to a full month triggers the complete observance of both prayer and fasting, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view on the transition of legal status.
